extracted.intended_audience: local news reporters and independent creators considering or starting a Substack publication
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and selling points for starting, growing, and monetizing a local-news newsletter/publication on Substack, emphasizing low startup cost, audience-first editorial independence, and paid subscription revenue potential. Includes example success metrics from existing local Substacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero startup costs / no overhead
rubrics_metrics.description: It’s free to sign up and start publishing. Cover a beat with zero startup expenses, and no tech or design costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes minimal financial and technical barriers to launch: sign-up is free, no hosting/design/tech overhead. Repeated calls-to-action: 'Start a publication with no overhead.' and 'It takes only a minute and zero overhead to get started.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-first editorial model (prioritize your audience, not advertisers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize your audience, not advertisers. The subscription model guarantees editorial independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position Substack's subscription approach as a way for reporters to be loyal only to their readership; enables focus on 'quality more than inundation.' Anti-pattern: relying primarily on advertisers rather than readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetization via paid subscriptions with high creator revenue share
rubrics_metrics.description: When you're ready, you can add paid subscriptions and keep 90% of the revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit financial incentive: creators retain 90% of subscription revenue (platform takes remainder). Guideline for timing: add paid subscriptions 'when you're ready.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential to scale to teams and six-figure earnings
rubrics_metrics.description: Top reporters are building teams and earning six figures on Substack each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that successful local Substacks can expand beyond a solo operator into staffed teams and reach annual six-figure revenue; serves as a benchmark of high success/scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform ease-of-use so creators can focus on reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: “Substack reliably makes the hard stuff easy, so I can focus on connecting local communities every morning.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testimonial framing: platform is meant to remove technical friction so journalists can concentrate on content and community connection; implies ease supports consistent publishing cadence (e.g., daily).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover a local beat / focus on community reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover a beat with zero startup expenses... connect local communities every morning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages focused, beat-driven local reporting as the content strategy for a Substack local news publication; emphasizes regular, community-centered coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure success by subscriber and revenue milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of success metrics: The Edinburgh Minute — more than 20,000 subscribers; City Hall Watcher — 900 paying subscribers in two years; The Charlotte Ledger — on pace for $175,000 in annual revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides concrete example benchmarks (subscriber counts, paying-subscriber growth, annual revenue) as observable indicators of traction and success to aspire to or compare against.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revenue consistency compared to one-off freelance payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Substack replaces money he used to make selling one-off stories to other outlets — money he is happy to have, since it’s more consistent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions subscription income as more predictable and steady relative to irregular freelance payouts; suggests evaluating monetization on predictability as well as amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from corporate media structures; direct reader relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: The technology now exists to permit people like me to build a relationship with readers unmediated by existing corporate media structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames direct-to-reader publishing as both a philosophical and practical criterion: maintain editorial independence and reader relationships without corporate intermediaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for varied local-news backgrounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Local news reporters from diverse backgrounds (former paper editors, specialty local reporters, collections of writers) are launching successful Substacks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit guideline that Substack is appropriate for a range of practitioner profiles — from former mainstream journalists to niche local beat reporters — suggesting applicability across experience levels and formats.
